70e6aaa207a65eed4b4833d0696a7d4e130bda33.summary: Lookout describes KoSpy, an Android spyware family disguised as utility apps and distributed through Google Play and Firebase Firestore, aimed at Korean and English-speaking users. Lookout attributes it to the North Korean group ScarCruft (APT37) with medium confidence and notes ties to APT43 infrastructure. Samples date from March 2022 to March 2024. The apps were removed from Google Play and the Firebase projects deactivated.

70c8c187f3ec6aef60cd3daebad232a3290fbfbf.summary: Huntress researchers found that a sample BlackBerry described as an iOS LightSpy implant is a previously unreported macOS variant of the LightSpy spyware framework. The dropper loads encrypted plugin modules from a command server; ten macOS plugins cover browser history, keychains, cameras, screens, audio and shell commands. Development paths suggest two hosts. The sample was uploaded to VirusTotal from India, which the report calls a weak signal.

709785bd47268e1c63c794e8f6fc8b00105ec37d.summary: Article reporting that Japanese game publisher Bandai Namco confirmed a cyberattack on July 3, 2022 in which unauthorized access to internal systems of Asian group companies (excluding Japan) may have exposed customer data. The BlackCat (AlphV) ransomware operation had claimed the breach on its leak site. The report says a ransomware attack is more than likely, though Bandai Namco gave no technical details. The report says BlackCat is believed to be a rebrand of DarkSide and cites an FBI warning that it had breached at least 60 entities.
